newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African police seek Thai ship in death probe.
newsitem.headline: S.African police seek Thai ship in death probe.

text.p: South African police said on Thursday they had opened a manslaughter and attempted murder probe after charges by 11 West Africans that the captain of a Thai-registered cargo ship had abandoned them on a raft in mid- ocean.

The seven Nigerians and four Ghanaians were washed up on tiny Dyer Island off Cape Agulhas on Tuesday night after drifting in shark-infested seas for two days. They said a 12th man had fallen from the raft and drowned.
A police spokeswoman quoted the West Africans as saying the ship, the TCK Sunanta of Bangkok, was planning to refuel in Durban.
She said that if it did the captain would be questioned, but no arrest warrant had been issued yet.
The West Africans said they boarded the ship in Abidjan on January 2, paying the captain $2,000 each on the understanding they would work as crew and be given passage to the Far East.
But on January 12 the captain forced them overboard in mid- ocean with a raft made from oil drums, they said.
The men were found by a nature conservation official who lives on the island, an important breeding site for sea birds.

His department on Wednesday quoted the men as saying they were stowaways on a Taiwanese ship. There was no immediate explanation for apparent discrepancies between what the men told nature conservation officials and what they told police.
The West Africans are being held at a Cape Town jail and will be repatriated to their home countries, police said.
